text:
ravi: noticing p99 token latency climbing on dedicated-usw1-s33. top-talkers point to a single tenant causing sustained NIC egress and KV churn. looks like a regen loop. anyone free to triage?

zoe: can you paste the hot-host / tenant metrics and which host is hottest?

ravi: slice=dedicated-usw1-s33, hosts=rack-21-host4,rack-21-host5. metrics snippet:
```
nic_tx_tail_mbps{host="rack-21-host4"}=1420
kv_cache_miss_rate{tenant="dataflow-x"}=0.31
allocs_by_priority{slice="dedicated-usw1-s33"}={interactive:12, batch:84}
request_latency_p99{slice="dedicated-usw1-s33"}=195ms
```

kelly: classic hot-key prefetch + egress queue saturation. quick mitigation: (1) toggle tenant prefetch=false to stop aggressive KV regen, (2) soft-pin high-priority interactive allocs to alternate rack (rack-22), (3) apply a transient nic_tx shaper on the hot host. downside: extra failover cost and slightly higher cold-start for some interactives.

oncall: actions taken: prefetch toggled for tenant dataflow-x at 2024-11-15T11:02Z; nic_shaper 30% applied on rack-21-host4; evicted 20 best-effort batch pods from s33. ops-bot will watch.

ops-bot: action-log: prefetch=false tenant=dataflow-x by @oncall; nic_shaper applied on rack-21-host4; evicted pods=20; monitoring kv_cache_miss_rate and p99 every 30s.

zoe: after interventions p99 dropped to ~98ms. kv_miss down to 0.08. good short-term. we need a plan so the same tenant doesn't repeatedly trigger manual ops. proposal below.

ravi: curious what long-term policy looks like. important to balance reserved capacity cost and SLA.

kelly: proposal: adaptive fingerprint + economic deterrent. idea: fingerprint noisy behavior (signal: kv_miss_rate >0.2 && nic_tx_tail >1Gbps over 10m) then one of three actions depending on recurrence tier:
- Tier A (first offender): auto-toggle prefetch=false + route new low-priority allocs to fractional carveout (small reserved carve)
- Tier B (repeat within 7d): fractional carve with 50% reserved charge passed to tenant as surcharge + limit burst egress via proxy-stitching
- Tier C (persistent): move tenant to a dedicated mini-slab (longer reserved commitment) and apply billing penalty for operational overhead

Sample policy (plain text):
```
fingerprint_condition = kv_miss_rate > 0.2 AND nic_tx_tail > 1000 (10m)
on_detect:
  if occurrences == 1:
    actions: [toggle_prefetch(false), route_lowprio_fractional]
  elif occurrences <=3 within 7d:
    actions: [fractional_reserved(50%), apply_surcharge, proxy_stitch_lowprio]
  else:
    actions: [promote_to_mini_slab, ops_penalty_tag]
```

zoe: love it. two engineering notes: (1) need a simulation that models reserved-slice fill and cost transfer for top-20 noisy tenants, (2) ensure telemetry exposes "fingerprint_hits" metric and a per-tenant "operational-surcharge" flag so billing can reconcile.

oncall: i'll own the canary: simulate first, then run a 5% canary in us-west1 for 48h. rollback if cold-starts or p99 for other tenants worsen.

ravi: finance/commerce flag: if we add surcharges we need legal and sales sign-off for TOS changes. tagging @finance and @legal.

kelly: implementation checklist: (A) prefetch toggle endpoint for tenants (small API), (B) proxy-stitch route knob (dataplane), (C) fingerprint detector in telemetry pipeline + metric, (D) simulation job + cost model, (E) billing flag wiring. estimate ~2w across infra + billing + finance review.

zoe: i'll draft a short RFC with the cost model and rollout plan. ravi can you paste the 48h sim numbers once ready? cc @product for SLA language updates. :thumbsup:
